summary: Cecil Bendall was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and Oxford, learning under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge, where he became professor in 1903.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held appointments at Yale (~1949–1951) and the University of Chicago (~1967–1970) before serving as professor of English at the University of Virginia from ~1970 to 1991.

Ch'ing-mao Cheng studied at National Taiwan University and Princeton. A scholar in Sinology and Japanology, he taught at UC Berkeley (~1969–1976), chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst (~1976–1996), and was Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University (~1996–2003).

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaeson Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under the guidance of Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse.

Linguist Chaim Rabin studied at SOAS University of London (~1934–1939) and the University of Oxford (~1939–1943). He held academic posts at the University of Oxford from 1941 to 1956 and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1956 to 1986.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, conducted research at the University of Delhi and Kyoto University. As attested in 2015, he served as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago.

Working in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad earned a doctorate in philosophy at Oxford. He held research fellowships at Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Trinity College, Oxford, and served as professor at Lancaster University (attested 2000–2012).

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, active in religious and Buddhist studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and later attested as a lecturer there in 2009.

Historian Chandra R. de Silva served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991). He later served as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Indologist Chandrabhal Tripathi completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1957–1960) under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen (~1960–1976), the University of Cologne, and served as professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1976–1994).

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. During his studies, he was guided by Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and Noritoshi Aramaki. He served as professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1931–1949).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002) and studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002). His supervisors and teachers included Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.
Channa Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied as a PhD candidate at Leiden University (attested 2019) under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015).

Charlene Elizabeth Makley, a Tibetologist, completed her PhD at the University of Michigan in 1999 under doctoral supervisor Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She holds a post as associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Alexander Moore studied at Yale (AB ~1922–1926; PhD ~1926–1932). A philosopher, he taught at Yale (~1933–1936), was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1936–1967), and founded and edited Philosophy East and West (1951–~1967).
